mock_data.title: Discrimination against Disability
mock_data.passage:
Many of us are guilty of discriminating against disabled people, whether intentionally or not. People with disabilities are often treated extremely patronizingly by abled people, as though they were very young children. For example, a person in a wheelchair may be completely ignored and questions such as 'Does he want black or white coffee?' are put to a companion rather than directly to the person.

If people in wheelchairs can get around by themselves and so are able to travel alone, they are frequently treated as though they are invisible. Other people simply push rudely past them without paying any attention to them.

Obviously, people with disabilities will want to do the same things as able-bodied people. Thus, they will wish to visit museums, art galleries, restaurants and other public places. However, gaining access to such places can be far from easy. Often, the entrance to public buildings is at the top of some steps, which can prove to be an obstacle to someone who is in a wheelchair. Admittedly, some buildings now provide ramps, which makes life much easier.

Since doorways are often rather narrow, wheelchair-users have difficulty in negotiating them. Having succeeded in entering a building, disabled people might well meet another obstacle. The only means of getting from one floor to another, especially if it is an old building, might well be by a flight of stairs. Even if there is a lift as an alternative to the stairs, it may not be big enough to hold a wheelchair. One good thing about modern buildings is that they are usually equipped with reasonably roomy lifts, as well as escalators. This makes life easier for disabled people.

Nowadays, many disabled people are able to manage perfectly well at home by themselves. They might have a special lift to get to another floor, and a range of especially adapted appliances to help them fend for themselves.

It is when they attempt to go outside that obstacles to ordinary living begin. Society must do all in its power to remove these. Some provision is now being made for people with disabilities, but they need many more facilities. Otherwise society can be accused of ableism.
mock_data.passageB1:
Sometimes, people treat people with disabilities unfairly. This is called discrimination. It can happen even if we don't mean to do it. Sometimes people act like disabled people are children.

For example, imagine someone in a wheelchair. People might ask their friend, 'Does he want coffee?' instead of asking the person in the wheelchair directly. It's like they don't notice the person. Sometimes, people just walk past them without being careful.

People with disabilities want to do the same things as everyone else. They want to go to museums, restaurants, and other public places. But it can be hard for them to get into these places. Often, there are steps at the entrance, which can be a problem for someone in a wheelchair. Some buildings have ramps now, which makes it easier.

Doorways can be too small for wheelchairs. And inside, there might only be stairs to go to other floors. Even if there is a lift, it might not be big enough. New buildings usually have bigger lifts and escalators. This is better for disabled people.

Many disabled people can manage at home by themselves. They might have a special lift or adapted appliances to help them. But when they go outside, they face many problems.

We need to make things easier for them. Society should try to remove these problems. Some things are being done, but we need more. We need more facilities for people with disabilities. If we don't, we are being unfair to them. We need to respect everyone.
mock_data.passageB2:
It's easy to fall into the trap of discriminating against people with disabilities, sometimes without even realising it. Often, able-bodied individuals unintentionally patronise those with disabilities, treating them like children. For instance, instead of asking a wheelchair user directly what they'd like to drink, someone might ask their companion, effectively ignoring the person in the wheelchair. Even when disabled people are clearly independent and travelling alone, they can be made to feel invisible, as if they don't warrant basic consideration. People may simply push past them without a second glance.

Naturally, disabled people have the same desires and interests as everyone else. They want to visit cultural attractions like museums and art galleries, eat out at restaurants, and generally participate in public life. However, gaining access to these places can present significant challenges. Public buildings often have steps at the entrance, which pose a considerable obstacle for wheelchair users. While some buildings now offer ramps, making access easier, this isn't always the case.

Narrow doorways can also be difficult to manoeuvre through for wheelchair users. Even after entering a building, further difficulties may arise. In older buildings, the only way to reach different floors might be a flight of stairs. Even if a lift is available, it might be too small to accommodate a wheelchair. Modern buildings are generally better equipped, usually featuring reasonably spacious lifts and escalators, which significantly improve accessibility for disabled people.

Many disabled people are perfectly capable of living independently at home. They might have a lift installed to access different floors, and a range of specially adapted appliances to help them manage everyday tasks. However, the moment they venture outside, they encounter a multitude of barriers that hinder their ability to live a normal life. Society must make every effort to remove these barriers. While some progress has been made in providing facilities for people with disabilities, much more needs to be done. Failure to do so risks perpetuating ableism and further marginalising this group.
mock_data.passageC1:
It is lamentable how often, whether through conscious prejudice or sheer thoughtlessness, many of us are complicit in acts of discrimination against individuals with disabilities. A particularly galling manifestation of this is the patronizing manner in which able-bodied individuals frequently interact with those who are differently abled, often treating them as though they possess the cognitive capacity of young children. A case in point would be the common occurrence of addressing questions intended for a wheelchair user to their companion – queries such as coffee preferences – thereby effectively rendering the individual invisible. Indeed, even when wheelchair users demonstrably possess the independence to navigate public spaces alone, they are often subjected to the indignity of being ignored or, worse still, physically bypassed with a distinct lack of consideration.

It stands to reason that individuals with disabilities share the same aspirations and desires as their able-bodied counterparts, including the wish to partake in cultural and social activities. However, the simple act of accessing public amenities such as museums, galleries, and restaurants can prove to be an arduous undertaking. The architectural design of many buildings, particularly older structures, often presents significant barriers, with entrances located at the summit of staircases, thereby posing an insurmountable obstacle to wheelchair users. While the provision of ramps in some modern buildings undoubtedly represents progress, even these accommodations are frequently inadequate.

The challenges do not cease upon entering a building. Narrow doorways can present further difficulties for wheelchair users, and once inside, the absence of suitable elevators, particularly in older buildings, can effectively restrict access to upper floors. Even when lifts are available, their dimensions may be insufficient to accommodate a wheelchair, thereby perpetuating the exclusion of individuals with mobility impairments. The prevalence of spacious lifts and escalators in contemporary architecture offers a glimmer of hope, facilitating greater accessibility for disabled people.

While many disabled individuals are now equipped to manage independently within their own homes, often through the utilisation of specialised lifts and adapted appliances that foster self-sufficiency, it is upon venturing into the public sphere that the most formidable obstacles to ordinary living arise. Society has a moral imperative to dismantle these barriers with all available resources. Although some provisions are currently in place, a far greater expansion of facilities is urgently required. Failure to do so renders society vulnerable to the accusation of ableism, a systemic prejudice that undermines the dignity and autonomy of individuals with disabilities, thereby impeding their full participation in civic life. Indeed, it is time for society to address the root causes of this inequity and foster a culture of inclusivity.

mock_data.translation:
Ko'pchiligimiz, qasddan bo'ladimi yoki yo'qmi, nogironligi bo'lgan shaxslarni kamsitishda (discriminating) aybdormiz. Nogironligi bo'lgan odamlarga (People with disabilities) ko'pincha sog'lom odamlar (abled) tomonidan, xuddi yosh bolalardek, juda past nazar bilan (patronizingly) munosabatda bo'lishadi. Masalan, nogironlar aravachasidagi kishi butunlay e'tibordan chetda qolishi mumkin va 'U qora yoki sutli kofe xohlaydimi?' kabi savollar bevosita kishining o'ziga emas, balki uning hamrohiga (companion) beriladi.

Agar nogironlar aravachasidagi odamlar o'zlari harakatlana olsalar va shuning uchun yolg'iz sayohat qila olsalar, ularga ko'pincha xuddi ular ko'rinmasdek (invisible) munosabatda bo'lishadi. Boshqa odamlar ularga hech qanday e'tibor bermasdan, shunchaki qo'pollik bilan yonlaridan itarib o'tib ketishadi.

Shubhasiz, nogironligi bo'lgan odamlar ham sog'lom (able-bodied) odamlar kabi bir xil ishlarni qilishni xohlashadi. Shunday qilib, ular muzeylar, san'at galereyalari, restoranlar va boshqa jamoat joylariga tashrif buyurishni xohlashadi. Biroq, bunday joylarga kirish (access) imkoniyatiga ega bo'lish oson bo'lmasligi mumkin. Ko'pincha, jamoat binolarining kirish qismi bir nechta zinapoyalar tepasida joylashgan bo'lib, bu nogironlar aravachasidagi kishi uchun to'siq (obstacle) bo'lib xizmat qilishi mumkin. Tan olish kerakki, ba'zi binolar endi panduslar (ramps) bilan ta'minlangan, bu esa hayotni ancha osonlashtiradi.

Eshik o'rinlari (doorways) ko'pincha juda tor bo'lganligi sababli, nogironlar aravachasidan foydalanuvchilar ulardan o'tishda (negotiating) qiynalishadi. Binoga kirishga muvaffaq bo'lgach, nogiron odamlar yana bir to'siqqa uchrashlari mumkin. Bir qavatdan (floor) boshqasiga o'tishning yagona yo'li, ayniqsa u eski bino bo'lsa, zinapoyalar bo'lishi mumkin. Zinapoyalarga muqobil sifatida lift mavjud bo'lsa ham, u nogironlar aravachasini sig'dirish uchun etarli darajada katta bo'lmasligi mumkin. Zamonaviy binolarning yaxshi tomoni shundaki, ular odatda etarli darajada keng (roomy) liftlar, shuningdek, eskalarorlar bilan jihozlangan (equipped with). Bu nogironlar uchun hayotni osonlashtiradi.

Hozirgi kunda nogironligi bo'lgan ko'plab odamlar uyda o'zlari mustaqil ravishda ishlarini boshqara oladilar. Ularda boshqa qavatga chiqish uchun maxsus lift va ularga o'z-o'zini ta'minlashga (fend for themselves) yordam beradigan bir qator foydalanishga moslashtirilgan asbob-uskunalar (appliances) bo'lishi mumkin.

Aynan ular tashqariga chiqishga harakat qilganlarida oddiy hayot uchun to'siqlar boshlanadi. Jamiyat bularni bartaraf etish uchun qo'lidan kelgan barcha ishni qilishi kerak. Hozirda nogironligi bo'lgan odamlar uchun ba'zi choralar (provision) ko'rilmoqda, ammo ularga yana ko'proq sharoitlar (facilities) kerak. Aks holda jamiyatni eyblizmda (ableism - nogironlarni kamsitish) ayblash mumkin.

notice.definition: To see or become aware of something.

respect.definition: To treat someone with politeness and kindness.

escalators.example: Take the escalator to the next floor.

facilities.definition: Places or equipment provided for a particular purpose.

discrimination.definition: Treating someone unfairly because of who they are.

don't warrant.uzbek: Biror narsaga loyiq emas yoki kerak emas.
don't warrant.example: His behaviour doesn't warrant such a harsh punishment.
don't warrant.exampleUzbek: Uning xatti-harakatlari bunday qattiq jazoga loyiq emas.

gaining access.uzbek: Biror narsaga kirish yoki foydalanish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lish.
gaining access.example: Gaining access to the internet is essential for education.
gaining access.definition: The act of being able to enter or use something.

manoeuvre through.uzbek: Ehtiyotkorlik bilan biror narsani yoki kimnidir boshqarish yoki yo'naltirish, ayniqsa qiyin vaziyatda ularni ma'lum bir tarzda harakatlantirish yoki joylashtirish.
manoeuvre through.example: It was difficult to manoeuvre the car through the crowded streets.
manoeuvre through.definition: To carefully guide or direct something or someone in order to move or position them in a certain way, especially in a difficult situation.
manoeuvre through.exampleUzbek: Mashinani gavjum ko'chalarda boshqarish qiyin edi.

effectively ignoring.uzbek: Kimnidir e'tiborsiz qoldirish bilan bir xil natijaga ega bo'lish, hatto bu sizning maqsadingiz bo'lmasa ham.
effectively ignoring.example: By not responding to his emails, I was effectively ignoring him.
effectively ignoring.definition: Having the same result as if you were ignoring someone, even if that wasn't your intention.
effectively ignoring.exampleUzbek: Uning elektron pochta xabarlariga javob bermasdan, men uni e'tiborsiz qoldirayotgan edim.

perpetuating ableism.uzbek: Nogironligi bo'lgan odamlarga nisbatan kamsitish va adolatsizlikni qo'llab-quvvatlashni davom ettirish.
perpetuating ableism.example: By not providing accessible facilities, the company is perpetuating ableism.
perpetuating ableism.definition: Continuing to support discrimination and prejudice against people with disabilities.
perpetuating ableism.exampleUzbek: Qulayliklarni ta'minlamasdan, kompaniya nogironlarga nisbatan kamsitishni davom ettirmoqda.

fall into the trap of.uzbek: Qandaydir salbiy ishni beixtiyor qilib qo'yish yoki xato qilish.
fall into the trap of.example: It's easy to fall into the trap of judging people based on their appearance.
fall into the trap of.definition: To unintentionally do something negative or make a mistake.
fall into the trap of.exampleUzbek: Odamlarni tashqi ko'rinishiga qarab baholash oson.

multitude of barriers.uzbek: Biror narsaning sodir bo'lishiga yoki kimningdir rivojlanishiga to'sqinlik qiladigan juda ko'p narsalar.
multitude of barriers.example: She faced a multitude of barriers in her career.
multitude of barriers.definition: A very large number of things that prevent something from happening or someone from progressing.
multitude of barriers.exampleUzbek: U o'z faoliyatida ko'plab to'siqlarga duch keldi.

remove these barriers.uzbek: Kimningdir biror narsa qilishiga yoki rivojlanishiga to'sqinlik qilayotgan narsalardan xalos bo'lish.
remove these barriers.example: We need to remove these barriers to ensure equal opportunities.
remove these barriers.definition: To get rid of the things that are stopping someone from doing something or progressing.
remove these barriers.exampleUzbek: Teng imkoniyatlarni ta'minlash uchun biz bu to'siqlarni olib tashlashimiz kerak.

unintentionally patronise.uzbek: Kimnidir do'stona munosabatda bo'lish, lekin o'zingizni ulardan yaxshiroq yoki aqlliroq deb hisoblash; beixtiyor.
unintentionally patronise.example: I hope I didn't unintentionally patronise her by explaining something she already knew.
unintentionally patronise.definition: To treat someone in a way that appears friendly, but which shows that you think you are better or more intelligent than them; without meaning to.
unintentionally patronise.exampleUzbek: U biladigan narsani tushuntirib berib, uni beixtiyor kamsitib qo'ymadimmi deb umid qilaman.

pose a considerable obstacle.example: The language barrier posed a considerable obstacle to communication.
pose a considerable obstacle.definition: To create a significant problem or difficulty.
pose a considerable obstacle.exampleUzbek: Til to'sig'i aloqaga katta to'siq bo'ldi.

significantly improve accessibility.uzbek: Biror narsaga kirish yoki foydalanishni ancha osonlashtirish.
significantly improve accessibility.example: The new ramp significantly improved accessibility for wheelchair users.
significantly improve accessibility.definition: To make something much easier to access or use.
significantly improve accessibility.exampleUzbek: Yangi pandus nogironlar aravachalari foydalanuvchilari uchun kirish imkoniyatini sezilarli darajada yaxshiladi.

ableism.uzbek: odatiy qobiliyatlar ustun degan e'tiqodga asoslangan nogironligi bo'lgan odamlarga nisbatan kamsitish va ijtimoiy xurofot.
ableism.example: Ableism is a pervasive form of discrimination that needs to be addressed.
ableism.definition: Discrimination and social prejudice against people with disabilities based on the belief that typical abilities are superior.
ableism.exampleUzbek: Ableizm - hal qilinishi kerak bo'lgan kamsitishning keng tarqalgan shakli.

effectively rendering.uzbek: amalda kimnidir yoki nimanidir ko'rinmas yoki ahamiyatsiz qilib qo'yish.
effectively rendering.example: The new regulations are effectively rendering small businesses unable to compete.
effectively rendering.definition: Having the practical result of making someone or something invisible or unimportant.
effectively rendering.exampleUzbek: Yangi qoidalar kichik bizneslarning raqobatlasha olmasligiga olib kelmoqda.

undermines the dignity.uzbek: kimningdir qadr-qimmati va hurmat tuyg'usini susaytiradi yoki buzadi.
undermines the dignity.example: Poverty undermines the dignity of individuals and communities.
undermines the dignity.definition: Weakens or damages the sense of worth and respect of someone.
undermines the dignity.exampleUzbek: Qashshoqlik shaxslar va jamiyatlarning qadr-qimmatini pasaytiradi.

address the root causes.uzbek: muammoning asosiy yoki eng asosiy sabablarini hal qilish.
address the root causes.example: To solve this issue, we need to address the root causes of poverty.
address the root causes.definition: Deal with the fundamental or most basic reasons for a problem.
address the root causes.exampleUzbek: Ushbu muammoni hal qilish uchun biz qashshoqlikning asosiy sabablarini hal qilishimiz kerak.

foster self-sufficiency.uzbek: boshqalarga tayanmasdan o'ziga g'amxo'rlik qilish qobiliyatini rivojlantirish yoki rag'batlantirish.
foster self-sufficiency.example: Education programs should foster self-sufficiency in young people.
foster self-sufficiency.definition: Promote or encourage the ability to take care of oneself without relying on others.
foster self-sufficiency.exampleUzbek: Ta'lim dasturlari yoshlarda o'ziga ishonchni shakllantirishi kerak.

dismantle these barriers.uzbek: taraqqiyotga yoki tenglikka to'sqinlik qiladigan to'siqlarni olib tashlash yoki demontaj qilish.
dismantle these barriers.example: We need to dismantle these barriers to ensure equal opportunities for all.
dismantle these barriers.definition: Remove or take apart obstacles that prevent progress or equality.
dismantle these barriers.exampleUzbek: Barcha uchun teng imkoniyatlarni ta'minlash uchun biz ushbu to'siqlarni bartaraf etishimiz kerak.

accessing public amenities.uzbek: ommaviy foydalanish uchun mavjud bo'lgan imkoniyatlarga kirish va ulardan foydalanish.
accessing public amenities.example: Accessing public amenities should be a right, not a privilege.
accessing public amenities.definition: Gaining entry to and using facilities available for public use.
accessing public amenities.exampleUzbek: Ommaviy qulayliklardan foydalanish huquq bo'lishi kerak, imtiyoz emas.

perpetuating the exclusion.uzbek: kimnidir chetlashtirish yoki marginalizatsiya qilish holatini davom ettirish yoki uzaytirish.
perpetuating the exclusion.example: Stereotypes can perpetuate the exclusion of certain groups from society.
perpetuating the exclusion.definition: Continuing or prolonging the state of someone being left out or marginalized.
perpetuating the exclusion.exampleUzbek: Stereotiplar jamiyatdan ma'lum guruhlarni chetlashtirishni davom ettirishi mumkin.

foster a culture of inclusivity.uzbek: hamma o'zini qadrlaydigan, hurmat qiladigan va qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan muhitni rag'batlantirish va rivojlantirish.
foster a culture of inclusivity.example: The company is working to foster a culture of inclusivity and diversity.
foster a culture of inclusivity.definition: Promote and develop an environment where everyone feels valued, respected, and supported.
foster a culture of inclusivity.exampleUzbek: Kompaniya inklyuzivlik va xilma-xillik madaniyatini rivojlantirish ustida ishlamoqda.

impeding their full participation.uzbek: kimningdir faoliyatda yoki jamiyatda to'liq ishtirok etishiga to'sqinlik qilish yoki xalaqit berish.
impeding their full participation.example: Lack of accessibility is impeding their full participation in social life.
impeding their full participation.definition: Preventing or hindering someone from fully engaging in activities or society.
impeding their full participation.exampleUzbek: Qulaylikning yo'qligi ularning ijtimoiy hayotda to'liq ishtirok etishiga to'sqinlik qilmoqda.

posing an insurmountable obstacle.example: The lack of funding is posing an insurmountable obstacle to the project's completion.
posing an insurmountable obstacle.definition: Creating a barrier that cannot be overcome.
posing an insurmountable obstacle.exampleUzbek: Mablag'ning yetishmasligi loyihaning yakunlanishiga yengib bo'lmaydigan to'siq bo'lmoqda.

complicit in acts of discrimination.uzbek: kamsitish harakatlarida ishtirok etish yoki ularga hissa qo'shish, hatto beixtiyor ham.
complicit in acts of discrimination.example: By remaining silent, we are all complicit in acts of discrimination against marginalized groups.
complicit in acts of discrimination.definition: Involved in or contributing to discriminatory actions, even unintentionally.
complicit in acts of discrimination.exampleUzbek: Sukut saqlash orqali biz barcha chetlashtirilgan guruhlarga nisbatan kamsitish harakatlarida ishtirok etamiz.

a particularly galling manifestation.uzbek: Biror narsaning ayniqsa g'azablantiruvchi yoki qo'zg'atuvchi namunasi.
a particularly galling manifestation.example: The blatant disregard for the rules was a particularly galling manifestation of their arrogance.
a particularly galling manifestation.definition: An especially irritating or provoking example of something.
a particularly galling manifestation.exampleUzbek: Qoidalarga ochiqchasiga bepisand bo'lish ularning takabburligining ayniqsa g'azablantiruvchi namoyishi edi.

mock_data.translationB1:
Ba'zan odamlar nogironligi bor odamlarga nisbatan adolatsiz munosabatda bo'lishadi. Bu diskriminatsiya deb ataladi. Bu biz buni xohlamasak ham sodir bo'lishi mumkin. Ba'zida odamlar nogiron odamlarga go'yo ular bola bo'lganday muomala qilishadi.

Misol uchun, nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamni tasavvur qiling. Odamlar nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamdan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri so'rash o'rniga, ularning do'stidan: "U kofe xohlami?" deb so'rashlari mumkin. Go'yo ular odamni payqashmayotganday. Ba'zan odamlar ularning yonidan ehtiyot bo'lmasdan shunchaki o'tib ketishadi.

Nogironligi bor odamlar boshqalar kabi bir xil narsalarni qilishni xohlashadi. Ular muzeylarga, restoranlarga va boshqa jamoat joylariga borishni xohlashadi. Ammo ularga bu joylarga kirish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Ko'pincha, kirish joyida zinapoyalar bo'ladi, bu nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odam uchun muammo bo'lishi mumkin. Ba'zi binolarda hozir panduslar bor, bu esa vaziyatni osonlashtiradi.

Eshiklar nogironlar aravachalari uchun juda kichik bo'lishi mumkin. Ichkarida esa boshqa qavatlarga chiqish uchun faqat zinapoyalar bo'lishi mumkin. Hatto lift bo'lsa ham, u yetarlicha katta bo'lmasligi mumkin. Yangi binolarda odatda kattaroq liftlar va eskalaторlar bo'ladi. Bu nogironlar uchun yaxshiroqdir.

Ko'p nogiron odamlar uyda o'zlari boshqara olishadi. Ularda maxsus lift yoki ularga yordam beradigan moslashtirilgan jihozlar bo'lishi mumkin. Ammo ular tashqariga chiqqanda, ular ko'plab muammolarga duch kelishadi.

Biz ular uchun vaziyatni osonlashtirishimiz kerak. Jamiyat bu muammolarni bartaraf etishga harakat qilishi kerak. Ba'zi ishlar qilinmoqda, ammo bizga ko'proq narsa kerak. Bizga nogironligi bor odamlar uchun ko'proq qulayliklar kerak. Agar biz buni qilmasak, ularga nisbatan adolatsiz munosabatda bo'lamiz. Biz hammaga hurmat ko'rsatishimiz kerak.

Nogironligi bor insonlarga nisbatan kamsitish tuzog'iga tushib qolish oson, ba'zan buni anglamasdan ham. Masalan, nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamdan nima ichishni xohlashini to'g'ridan-to'g'ri so'rash o'rniga, kimdir ularning hamrohidan so'rashi mumkin, bu nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamni e'tiborsiz qoldirishga teng. Nogironlar mustaqil ekanligi va yolg'iz sayohat qilayotgani aniq bo'lsa ham, ular ko'rinmas bo'lib qolishlari mumkin, go'yo ular asosiy e'tiborga loyiq emasdek. Odamlar shunchaki ularning yonidan o'tib ketishlari mumkin.

Tabiiyki, nogironlar ham boshqa har bir kishi kabi xohish va manfaatlariga ega. Ular muzeylar va san'at galereyalari kabi madaniy obidalarga tashrif buyurishni, restoranlarda ovqatlanishni va umuman olganda ijtimoiy hayotda ishtirok etishni xohlashadi. Biroq, bu joylarga kirish jiddiy muammolarni keltirib chiqarishi mumkin. Jamoat binolarining kirish joylarida ko'pincha zinapoyalar bo'ladi, bu nogironlar aravachasi foydalanuvchilari uchun katta to'siqni hosil qiladi. Hozirda ba'zi binolar panduslar bilan ta'minlangan bo'lsa-da, bu har doim ham shunday emas.

Tor eshiklardan nogironlar aravachasida o'tish ham qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Binoga kirgandan keyin ham, qo'shimcha qiyinchiliklar paydo bo'lishi mumkin. Eski binolarda turli qavatlarga chiqishning yagona yo'li zinapoya bo'lishi mumkin. Agar lift mavjud bo'lsa ham, u nogironlar aravachasini sig'dira olmaydigan darajada kichik bo'lishi mumkin. Zamonaviy binolar odatda yaxshiroq jihozlangan bo'lib, odatda keng liftlar va eskalatorlar mavjud bo'lib, ular nogironlar uchun qulaylikni sezilarli darajada oshiradi.

Ko'pgina nogironlar uyda mustaqil yashashga qodir. Ular turli qavatlarga chiqish uchun o'rnatilgan liftga ega bo'lishi mumkin va kundalik vazifalarni bajarishga yordam beradigan maxsus moslashtirilgan jihozlarga ega bo'lishi mumkin. Biroq, ular tashqariga chiqqan zahoti, normal hayot kechirish qobiliyatiga to'sqinlik qiladigan ko'plab to'siqlarga duch kelishadi. Jamiyat bu to'siqlarni bartaraf etish uchun barcha sa'y-harakatlarni qilishi kerak. Nogironlar uchun sharoit yaratishda muayyan yutuqlarga erishilgan bo'lsa-da, hali ko'p ishlar qilinishi kerak. Aks holda, bu ableizmni davom ettirish va bu guruhni yanada chetlashtirish xavfini tug'diradi.

Afsuski, ko'pincha ongli ravishda kamsitish yoki shunchaki beparvolik tufayli ko'pchiligimiz nogironligi bo'lgan shaxslarga nisbatan kamsitish harakatlarida ishtirok etamiz. Bunga ayniqsa achinarli misol shuki, jismonan sog'lom odamlar nogironligi bo'lganlar bilan o'zaro munosabatda bo'lganda, ularni go'yo yosh bolalarning aqliy qobiliyatiga ega deb hisoblaydigan darajada past nazar bilan qarashadi. Misol uchun, nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamga berilishi kerak bo'lgan savollarni uning hamrohiga berish – masalan, qahva afzalliklari haqidagi savollar – shu orqali odamni amalda ko'rinmas holga keltirish keng tarqalgan hodisa. Haqiqatan ham, nogironlar aravachasida o'tirgan odamlar jamoat joylarida mustaqil ravishda harakatlanishga qodir ekanliklarini namoyish qilsalar ham, ular ko'pincha e'tiborga olinmaslik yoki undan ham yomoni, beparvolik bilan jismonan chetlab o'tilish kabi haqoratlarga duch kelishadi.

Nogironligi bo'lgan shaxslar jismonan sog'lom odamlar kabi xuddi shunday intilish va istaklarga ega ekanligi, shu jumladan madaniy va ijtimoiy tadbirlarda ishtirok etish istagi ham tabiiy. Biroq, muzeylar, galereyalar va restoranlar kabi jamoat joylariga kirishning oddiygina harakati ham qiyin vazifa bo'lishi mumkin. Ko'pgina binolarning, ayniqsa eski inshootlarning me'moriy dizayni ko'pincha sezilarli to'siqlarni keltirib chiqaradi, kirish joylari zinapoyalarning tepasida joylashgan bo'lib, bu nogironlar aravachasida o'tirganlar uchun hal qilib bo'lmaydigan to'siqni keltirib chiqaradi. Ba'zi zamonaviy binolarda panduslarning ta'minlanishi, shubhasiz, taraqqiyotni anglatadi, ammo bu qulayliklarning o'zi ham ko'pincha yetarli emas.

Muammolar binoga kirgandan keyin tugamaydi. Tor eshiklar nogironlar aravachasida o'tirganlar uchun qo'shimcha qiyinchiliklar tug'dirishi mumkin, va ichkarida tegishli liftlarning yo'qligi, ayniqsa eski binolarda, yuqori qavatlarga kirishni amalda cheklashi mumkin. Hatto liftlar mavjud bo'lganda ham, ularning o'lchamlari nogironlar aravachasini sig'dira olmasligi mumkin, shu bilan harakatlanish qobiliyati cheklangan shaxslarni cheklashni davom ettiradi. Zamonaviy me'morchilikda keng liftlar va eskalatorlarning keng tarqalishi nogironlar uchun yanada qulaylik yaratishga umid uyg'otadi.

Ko'pgina nogironlar hozirda o'z uylarida mustaqil ravishda yashashga qodir, ko'pincha maxsus liftlar va o'zini o'zi ta'minlashga yordam beradigan moslashtirilgan jihozlardan foydalanish orqali, lekin odamlarning oldiga chiqqanda hayotning eng katta to'siqlari paydo bo'ladi. Jamiyatda bu to'siqlarni bartaraf etish uchun barcha mavjud resurslardan foydalanish axloqiy burchdir. Hozirda ba'zi qoidalar mavjud bo'lsa-da, qulayliklarni yanada kengaytirishga zudlik bilan ehtiyoj bor. Aks holda, jamiyat ableizmda ayblanishi mumkin, bu nogironligi bo'lgan shaxslarning qadr-qimmatini va avtonomiyasini buzadigan va shu bilan ularning fuqarolik hayotida to'liq ishtirok etishiga to'sqinlik qiladigan tizimli kamsitishdir. Haqiqatan ham, jamiyat ushbu tengsizlikning asosiy sabablarini bartaraf etishi va inklyuzivlik madaniyatini rivojlantirishi vaqti keldi.
